The Archive Inspection Protocol (AIP) operates as a dual-state mechanism: it enforces read-only access (R) to ensure integrity while parsing embedded calibration briefs (B). The method valuation duality (MVD) arises from comparing PDF-based valuations against those derived from briefs, creating a duality gap (D) that quantifies undervaluation. Checkout validation (CV) ensures that any discovered methods are either present in the live system (L=1) or require import from the archive. These primitives form a closed-loop system where AIP feeds into MVD, which then validates against CV, ensuring method consistency across layers. Failure modes include R=0 (write access), D>threshold (undervaluation), and L=0 (missing method).
